findings.description: In a dispatched child, gate-answer compares only --approval-ref with the launch marker's gate_answer.approval_ref. It never checks --gate or --decision against gate_answer.gate/decision, so a child whose marker says {gate: proposal_approval, decision: rejected, approval_ref: R} can run gate-answer --decision approved --approval-ref R (or answer a different pending gate, or clear a park with a pending_gate answer) and record a human-provenance approval the supervisor never made. The spec requires the child to apply a gate decision only from the marker's gate_answer (skill-workflow 'Gate Authority and Re-Evaluation on Resume', design D5).
findings.resolution: Re-verified resolved in round 2: 5b28e32: gate-answer in a dispatched child now also refuses (exit 2, nothing recorded) when --gate or --decision differs from the marker's gate_answer; the check runs before both the pending-gate and the park path.

findings.description: The dispatched-child gate-answer tests cover only a mismatched approval_ref. No test pins that a matching approval_ref with a different --decision or --gate is refused, which is how finding 1 went unnoticed.
findings.resolution: Re-verified resolved in round 2: 5b28e32: test_a_matching_reference_does_not_authorize_another_gate_or_decision (flipped decision, other gate) and test_a_park_is_not_cleared_by_an_answer_for_another_gate assert exit 2 with loop-state.json byte-identical.

findings.description: apply_delegated_batch persists a permission_blocked result's parked.command verbatim: _terminal_attempt copies result['parked'] into the checkpoint attempt, and the application journal stores the whole result. Only the router's gate-decision record (parked_commands) is re-sanitized. checkpoint.json is a tracked file on a shared ref, and a result that did not come through runner.py park (hand-written, or from an older worker) can carry an unredacted credential; the apply-time re-derivation compares only the fingerprint (tool, rule, classifier_reason), not the command. Design D9 says the command is 're-sanitized by the router', and the supervise scenario requires the persisted command not to contain the secret. test_a_secret_in_the_blocked_command_is_redacted seeds the checkpoint attempt with the raw 'Bearer abc123...' value and checks only the record.
findings.resolution: Re-verified resolved in round 2: b34c6af: apply_delegated_batch redacts a non-null parked.command through dispatch_contract.redact_command right after ensure_v2_result, before binding, journaling and _terminal_attempt, so neither the attempt nor the journal holds the raw value.

findings.description: No test applies a permission_blocked result carrying a secret-bearing command and asserts that the persisted checkpoint (the attempt's parked payload and its application journal) contains no raw secret.
findings.resolution: Re-verified resolved in round 2: b34c6af: test_apply_never_persists_a_raw_blocked_command applies a Bearer-token command and asserts the secret is absent from checkpoint.json bytes and the journal copy equals the redacted attempt copy.

findings.description: redact_command is not idempotent for auth headers: backtracking in \s* defeats the (?!\[REDACTED:) lookahead, so re-redacting 'Authorization: [REDACTED:auth-header]' rewrites it to 'Authorization:[REDACTED:auth-header]'. Harmless for secrecy, but the router's second pass changes already-redacted text.
findings.resolution: Re-verified resolved in round 2: bad6de9: header lookahead is (?!\s*\[REDACTED:); re-redacting an already-redacted header is now a no-op (verified on bearer, URL userinfo, -u, keyed-secret samples).

findings.description: Carried from IMPL_ITERATE: in a dispatched child whose posture digest drifted, a notify_with_timeout gate can still take its posture-derived timeout default; the spec forbids only auto there.
Carried from IMPL_ITERATE: emit-result does not cross-check --dispatch-id/--generation against the launch marker; the supervisor's identity check still rejects a mismatch at apply.
Carried from IMPL_ITERATE: rebind accepts a post-go attempt with no recorded evidence when only a worktree for its branch exists on this host (the evidence conditions hold vacuously).

_resolve_capability_park's proceed path falls back to records[0] when the attempt is not among the fingerprint's parked members (its checkpoint copy moved on); with no members that raises IndexError instead of a GateRefusalError.
